images.title: A honeycomb tiling
images.purpose: Show a section of honeycomb, where bees tile space with regular hexagons and leave no gaps.
images.composition: A close view of a honeycomb filling most of the frame.
exact_structure: A flat illustration of a honeycomb made of regular hexagonal cells, about 5 rows of 6 cells, all the same size, with no gaps between them.
The cells are filled in amber (#E69F00) with dark outlines; a few cells are drawn a little lighter.
One small simple bee in the lower right corner.
The caption honeycomb under the picture.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Bees build with hexagons because hexagons tile the plane with no wasted space.
images.description: Show a section of honeycomb, where bees tile space with regular hexagons and leave no gaps.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.

image_decisions.why: A real world example makes the plane tilings feel familiar.
